# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `node_layout` against input/. See tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json for
# how to read this file, the _env/_settings convention and the ownership note.
#
# THIS CASE: Layout::Remote, and THE SETTING IS WHAT DECIDES IT (DESIGN.md v5.2, §2m.1). The mode is
# `node.mode = remote` with a valid `node.remote`, while input/systemctl.txt deliberately still shows
# fmonero-monerod.service present and ACTIVE -- so a detector that reads only the unit file answers
# user_unit, and this is the only case that catches it.
#
# REWRITTEN FOR v5.2. Until then the case keyed Remote on a NON-LOOPBACK `node.url` and expected
# `warn:non_loopback_url`, because §2c made such a URL an error for every client. That layout was
# unreachable through the CLI -- `settings set node.url` refuses every value that would produce it
# -- so the fixture was asserting a warning about a state the tool could not enter. §2m.1 re-keys
# the variant on `node.mode`, which is a supported configuration, and §7.1 therefore makes
# `node_layout` the one `node` check that still runs in remote mode and **passes**: it is the
# group's only remaining source of truth, so that `doctor --only node` is never an empty table.
#
# THE DETAIL MUST NAME THE ADDRESS, the trust flag and the ssl mode, because those three are what
# `units::daemon_target` put into the wallet unit's argv and into `set_daemon` -- and because a
# remote node is reached by monero-wallet-rpc, NOT by fmonero, which speaks plaintext HTTP to
# loopback only and contains no TLS stack at all (§2c, unchanged by v5.2).
# `fixable` is false: which node to use is the user's decision, and `fmonero node local --yes` is
# the runnable command the verdict names.
# `_probe.monerod_installed` stays true so that the case tests the layout arm rather than the
# `skip:monerod_not_installed` precondition in front of it.
# v5.6 (§2o): `node_layout`'s DETAIL is now plain language and the check's `id`, `group`,
# `severity`, `class`, `status` and `fixable` are unchanged -- which is the whole point of the
# rewrite: `--json` is the agent contract and this fixture pins it. What changed is the prose,
# so `detail_contains` names the words a person now reads. The internal layout words
# (`user_unit`, `system_unit`, `remote`, `none`), the trust flag and the ssl mode are gone from
# every human surface and stay in the payload.
